target_customer: Booking agencies, artist managers, talent buyers and independent artists in live music and events
problem: Concert booking ran on Word offer letters, PDF riders, faxes and physical checks, so agents lost time and tracking.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription priced by user count
product_category: Booking and gig management software for live entertainment

founders.name: Jeremie Habib
founders.background_notes: YC page says senior sales and business development roles at Cisco and early stage SaaS companies including OpenDNS; TechCrunch 2016 says he started by helping book DJs for a San Francisco nightclub.

founders.name: Glade Luco
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder on the YC page.

founders.name: Antonio Sierra
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Contract builders, payment collection and a venue database are standard SaaS work; the difficulty was domain workflow knowledge rather than engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Once an agency moves its offers, contracts and venue data in, it is costly to leave; the product itself was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response was found in the sources reviewed; Gigwell bought two assets from Jamplify in September 2017 (YC page news item citing Billboard).

market_need_then: TechCrunch on March 8, 2016 describes agents using Word offers, PDF riders, faxes and bank trips for payment, and customers including booking agencies Diplomats of Sound and Surefire.

branding.domain_note: Uses gigwell.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.visual_style: Dashboard screenshots, product icons, bold all caps section labels
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, confident and conversational with imperatives such as ditch the spreadsheets, fax machines and paper checks

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage in TechCrunch, Billboard and Hypebot; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: A functional name with trade press coverage in a niche B2B market; no source shows the brand as a growth driver.

pivots.from: Software for agencies and talent buyers
pivots.to: Also opened booking tools to artists and independent promoters
pivots.why: Per a Hypebot headline listed on the YC page; reason not read.

outcome_analysis: Gigwell raised about 1.3M from angels around its March 2016 launch and has stayed a small, independent vertical SaaS business with a team of 12 listed on the YC page. It claims over 100,000 users and 5 billion dollars in bookings, though those figures are company reported. No large venture round or exit was found, so the outcome looks like a modest steady business rather than a breakout, with the music booking niche limiting size.
notes: Aggregators disagree on funding: CB Insights shows 120K from YC in March 2016, Employbl lists a 1M seed from Comcast Ventures and other amounts totaling 1.77M; none recorded because only aggregators. The 1.3M figure comes from the TechCrunch article only (no second outlet found), so it is recorded with that single source and coverage is partial. Competitors left empty: the TechCrunch article names no rivals and rival lists (Stagent, SystemOne and others) come from undated or 2026 pages. The YC page lists no funding and the company site names no founders.
